notes: Identity verified from the supplied text: title An Inkblot for Attitudes: Affect Misattribution as Implicit Measurement; B. Keith Payne, Clara Michelle Cheng, Olesya Govorun, and Brandon D. Stewart; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2005, 89(3), 277–293; DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.89.3.277. Text contains the primary empirical report, Experiments 1–6 and references/appendix; not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied, so no rendering was possible. Assigned fields only. On pp. 280–281, the warning-condition simple priming test is F(2, 30) = 4.67, p < .02; the Prime × Warning interaction is F(2, 60) = 0.40, p = .68. The overall prime-valence main effect is F(2, 60) = 10.18, p < .01, and the no-warning simple effect is F(2, 30) = 5.62, p < .01. These are separate tests. The neutral description and page locator do not uniquely distinguish priming under warning from resistance to warning (interaction). No target was selected by numeric matching or row order. Candidate statistics and their same-test p bounds are preserved here only; no conversion performed.
